A [[linear differential operator]] ''L'' is called '''quasi-exactly-solvable''' ('''QES''') if it has a [[finite-dimensional]] [[invariant subspace]] of [[function (mathematics)|functions]] <math>\{\mathcal{V}\}_n</math> such that <math>L: \{\mathcal{V}\}_n \rightarrow \{\mathcal{V}\}_n,</math> where ''n'' is a [[Dimension (mathematics)|dimension]] of <math>\{\mathcal{V}\}_n</math>. There are two important cases:
# <math>\{\mathcal{V}\}_n</math> is the [[Space (mathematics)|space]] of [[multivariate polynomial]]s of degree not higher than some [[integer]] number; and
# <math>\{\mathcal{V}\}_n</math> is a subspace of a [[Hilbert space]]. Sometimes, the [[functional space]] <math>\{\mathcal{V}\}_n</math> is [[isomorphism (algebra)|isomorphic]] to the finite-dimensional [[representation space]] of a [[Lie algebra]] ''g'' of [[first-order differential operator]]s. In this case, the [[Operator (mathematics)|operator]] ''L'' is called a ''g''-Lie-algebraic Quasi-Exactly-Solvable operator. Usually, one can indicate basis where ''L'' has block-triangular form. If the operator ''L'' is of the [[Second-order differential equation|second order]] and has the form of the [[Schrödinger operator]], it is called a Quasi-Exactly-Solvable Schrödinger operator.

The most studied cases are [[one-dimensional]] <math>sl(2)</math>-Lie-algebraic quasi-exactly-solvable (Schrödinger) operators. The best known example is the sextic QES anharmonic oscillator with the Hamiltonian

<math>\{\mathcal{H}\} = -\frac{d^2}{dx^2} + a^2 x^6 + 2abx^4 + [b^2 - (4 n + 3 + 2p) a] x^2, \ a \geq 0\ ,\ n\in\mathbb{N}\ ,\ p=\{0,1\},</math>

where (''n+1'') [[eigenstate]]s of positive (negative) parity can be found [[algebra]]ically. Their [[eigenfunction]]s are of the form

<math>\Psi (x)\ =\ x^p P_n(x^2) e^{-\frac{a x^4}{4} - \frac{b x^2}{2} } \ ,</math>

where <math>P_n(x^2)</math> is a [[polynomial]] of degree ''n'' and (energies) [[eigenvalue]]s are roots of an [[algebraic equation]] of degree (''n+1''). In general, twelve families of one-dimensional QES problems are known, two of them characterized by elliptic potentials.
